import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_15/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_15/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Join on 'State' as per operation history
df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="State", how="inner", suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Ensure columns have the exact target schema and types:
# Target Schema:
# ['State': string,
#  'Participation_x': string,
#  'English': float,
#  'Math_x': float,
#  'Reading': float,
#  'Science': float,
#  'Composite': float,
#  'Participation_y': string,
#  'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing': integer,
#  'Math_y': integer,
#  'Total': integer]

# Convert columns to correct types
df['State'] = df['State'].astype(str)

# Participation columns are strings with % sign, keep as is
df['Participation_x'] = df['Participation_x'].astype(str)
df['Participation_y'] = df['Participation_y'].astype(str)

# Numeric columns conversions
float_cols = ['English', 'Math_x', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite']
for col in float_cols:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype(float)

int_cols = ['Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math_y', 'Total']
for col in int_cols:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['State', 'Participation_x', 'English', 'Math_x', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite',
                  'Participation_y', 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math_y', 'Total']

df = df[target_columns]

# Write the final dataframe to the target path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_15/target_multisource.csv"
df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_15/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_15/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'State' column (inner join to keep only matching states)
result = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="State", how="inner")

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
result = result.rename(columns={
    "Participation_x": "Participation_x",  # from source0 Participation
    "Participation_y": "Participation_y",  # from source1 Participation
    "Participation_x": "Participation_x",
    "Participation_y": "Participation_y",
    "Participation": "Participation_x",  # source0 Participation -> Participation_x
    "Participation_y": "Participation_y",
    "Participation": "Participation_x",
    "Participation_y": "Participation_y"
})

# The merge automatically adds suffixes _x and _y for overlapping columns Participation and Math
# So rename Participation_x and Participation_y explicitly:
result = result.rename(columns={
    "Participation_x": "Participation_x",
    "Participation_y": "Participation_y",
    "Evidence-Based Reading and Writing": "Evidence-Based Reading and Writing",
    "Math_x": "Math_x",
    "Math_y": "Math_y",
    "Total": "Total",
    "English": "English",
    "Reading": "Reading",
    "Science": "Science",
    "Composite": "Composite"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[[
    "State",
    "Participation_x",
    "English",
    "Math_x",
    "Reading",
    "Science",
    "Composite",
    "Participation_y",
    "Evidence-Based Reading and Writing",
    "Math_y",
    "Total"
]]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_15/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
